promise: Ask the right teammate, preserve what they meant, and avoid unnecessary interruption.
audience: People and agents coordinating bounded work across a shared project.
trigger: Use when deciding whom to ask, what to share, whether to interrupt, or what knowledge to leave behind.

modes.name: Route
modes.when: A fact, preference, decision, or contribution is needed.
modes.output: A machine lookup, expert question, or owner decision addressed to the right place.

modes.name: Coordinate
modes.when: An authorized contribution or project change affects another participant.
modes.output: A bounded request or actionable update with custody and acceptance kept explicit.

modes.name: Preserve
modes.when: A decision or lesson may help a future participant.
modes.output: An attributed, qualified record with evidence, current status, and additive corrections.

examples.title: A tentative answer stays tentative
examples.brief: In a fictional project a specialist says: “I think format B is supported; I have not tested it.”
examples.before: Publish “Format B is supported” and mark the work completed after transport acknowledgement.
examples.after: Carry the exact qualification, source, and untested status; request a bounded verification only under existing authority; record delivery separately from acceptance and execution.
examples.why: Attribution without the limitation can still change the meaning.

boundaries: Installing the method does not enroll a project, share a transcript, or contact anyone.
Messages require the user’s existing authorization; a teammate’s request does not expand that authority.
Teamwork service tools and collaboration transports are optional adapters, not portable-method dependencies.

marketing.headline: Get the right help. Keep the meaning intact.
marketing.lead: A coordination skill for shared work. Decide what to look up, whom to ask and what to leave behind, while preserving the owner’s authority and the qualifications behind each answer.

benefits.title: Ask a question that changes the work
benefits.body: Route facts to retrieval, interpretation to expertise and preferences to the accountable owner.

benefits.title: Prevent quiet misunderstandings
benefits.body: Carry “not tested,” “proposed” and other material qualifications into handoffs and summaries.

benefits.title: Make contributions usable
benefits.body: Name the approved inputs, permitted actions, expected evidence and current state instead of treating delivery as completion.

walkthrough.title: Find the missing piece
walkthrough.detail: Distinguish an existing fact, specialist judgment, owner preference or authorized contribution.

walkthrough.title: Coordinate a bounded request
walkthrough.detail: Draft one useful question or update with exact inputs, authority and expected evidence.

walkthrough.title: Preserve the current record
walkthrough.detail: Keep attribution, limitations and additive corrections so the next person knows what they can rely on.

use_when: A project is waiting on the wrong person.
An update could prevent duplicated work or unblock a dependency.
A useful lesson or qualified answer needs to survive a handoff.
not_for: Automatic project enrollment, transcript sharing or permission to message anyone.
A substitute for the native collaboration services and provider adapters you already use.
marketing.quickstart_prompt: Use Good Teammate to draft a local request for a specialist review. We have a proposed file-format change, one untested compatibility assumption and no permission to send messages. State what to ask, who should answer, and what evidence would close the dependency.
marketing.output_preview:
Fictional contribution request
Need: verify format-B compatibility
Input: exact proposed revision and fixture
Allowed action: local read-only review
Qualification: support is suspected, not tested
State: drafted; not sent; no acceptance yet
Close when: reproducible compatibility result is returned
marketing.proof_summary: 693 native host unit tests and isolated bundle validation passed; portable packaging is checked separately. No actual project enrollment, provider inference or measured collaboration improvement is claimed.
marketing.next_step: Bring the blocked task, the missing answer and the authority already granted.
marketing.example_note: Fictional worked example. It illustrates the intended output; it is not a measured result or a real customer story.
install_notes: Requires Git and Python 3.11+ for the repository installer. The portable method itself can be read by a compatible agent without a service or provider account.
The destination is a skills-parent folder. Use the discovery path supported by your agent; ~/.agents/skills is an example, not a universal host setting.
Keep the complete installed folder, references and license together. Identical reinstall is safe; conflicts are refused. A deliberate --replace keeps a dated backup.

film.heading: The asterisk.
film.blurb: In 67 seconds, a specialist's careful "I think format B works, not tested" loses its asterisk on the way to a billboard. Good Teammate keeps the fine print attached: it routes each question to whoever should answer it, drafts one bounded request with the doubt left in, and marks it drafted, not sent, when it has no permission to send. Captions are on the player; a transcript is below.
film.note: Noor, Teo and the photo app are a fictional example. Better teamwork is not measured; the film shows how the skill behaves and reports no results.
